name: tests-half-redis-operator-reconciliation-lifecycle-52d4
instr:
Redis operator cannot currently present a uniform, generation-aware lifecycle view across Redis, RedisCluster, RedisReplication, and RedisSentinel. Make conditions, Kubernetes Events, reconcile results, and lifecycle metrics describe the same durable progressing, waiting, failed, or ready transition without changing controller behavior.

Publish lifecycle state only at observable work boundaries, distinguishing deletion, skips, dependency waits, failures, and successful completion without claiming work that did not run. Redis reports resource and dynamic-configuration progress without gaining periodic reconciliation. RedisCluster distinguishes scaling, failover, resharding, repair, convergence, and readiness. RedisReplication preserves ordered phases and polling. RedisSentinel preserves watch-driven dependencies while distinguishing linked-replication, disruption-budget, Service, StatefulSet, and healing outcomes.

Replace conditions by type, preserve unrelated and kind-specific status, reject observations older than the committed generation, and stale prior Ready state when a new generation progresses. Retry conflicts using freshly loaded typed status. Emit Events and metrics only after a successful commit. Each changed transition emits exactly one Event and metric increment; identical observations are silent. Preserve cluster state, reasons, replica counts, replication master and connection evidence, short-circuit behavior, errors, retry timing, and reconcile results.
